title: Colimit-preserving presheaf extensions have the Kan mapping property on intermediate full subcategories
statement:
Use the universes, quasicategories and coherent functor mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$. Let $D$ be a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory, put $\mathcal P(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U})$, and let $y:D\to\mathcal P(D)$ be $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$. Let $E\subseteq\mathcal P(D)$ be any replete full subcategory containing the essential image of $y$, with $y_E:D\to E$ the induced functor. Let $Z$ be a quasicategory admitting all $\mathcal U$-small colimits and let $H:\mathcal P(D)\to Z$ preserve them. For every coherent functor $G:E\to Z$, restriction along $y_E$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(E,Z)}(H|_E,G)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(D,Z)}(Hy,Gy_E).$$
This equivalence is natural in $H,G$ and in restriction to any other intermediate full subcategory. Thus every transformation $Hy\to Gy_E$ has a contractible space of extensions $H|_E\to G$, including all coherent compatibility homotopies. In particular the identity on $Gy_E$, after an identification $Hy\simeq Gy_E$, determines such a comparison transformation. No colimit preservation by $G$ and no closure of $E$ under colimits is assumed; $E$ may be large relative to $\mathcal U$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.5(1), Lemma 5.1.5.3 and Proposition 4.3.2.17 (with Corollary 4.3.2.16), printed pp. 325-327 and 284-285; restriction of the pointwise left Kan extension to an intermediate full subcategory has the same representable slice diagrams. Online source read, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical fact.

proof.text: Keep the original small universe $\mathcal U$ fixed and choose a larger containing universe $\mathcal W$ for all the categories and functor categories used below; in the two cited nodes take $\mathcal U\prime=\mathcal W$. This does not change $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ or the colimits required of $H$. The quasicategory $D$ is $\mathcal U$-small, so it fits in $\mathcal W$ and has $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces; the last assertion of the first paragraph of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], applied with $\mathcal E=D$, says that the Yoneda functor $y:D\to\mathcal P(D)$, $d\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_D(-,d)$, is fully faithful: the maps $\operatorname{Map}_D(d,d\prime)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(D)}(y(d),y(d\prime))$ are equivalences. Since $E$ is a full subcategory of $\mathcal P(D)$ containing every $y(d)$, its right-pinched mapping spaces between objects of $E$ are those of $\mathcal P(D)$, so the induced functor $y_E:D\to E$ is fully faithful. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] with $\mathcal X=D$ and $\mathcal Y=E$; both fit in $\mathcal W$, and that statement imposes no $\mathcal U$-smallness requirement on $E$. Obtain its full replete essential image $A\subseteq E$ and a coherent quasi-inverse $K:A\to D$, with coherent unit and counit equivalences.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.2, printed pp. 324-325, and Proposition 5.1.3.1, printed p. 320 (fully faithful Yoneda, stated in lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits); the coherent essential-image equivalence is the statement of lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image, not Corollary 4.3.2.16.

proof.text: For $c\in E$, write $F=c$ in $\mathcal P(D)$. The node [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-representable-slice-density] supplies the essentially $\mathcal U$-small slice $A_{/F}$ and its canonical colimiting cocone $\delta_F$. The full essential image $A$ of step 1 is precisely the $A$ in that node, since $E$ is full and replete and contains all representables. In every degree, a simplex of $A\times_E E_{/c}$ is a simplex of $\mathcal P(D)$ with initial face in $A$ and final vertex $c$. All its vertices belong to $E$, so fullness gives equality with $A_{/F}$, respecting every simplex operator and the appended-vertex cocone. Colimiting cocones in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] are exactly $p$-colimit diagrams for the map $p$ to $\Delta^0$: for $q:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ with boundary $f$, apex $x$ and coherent cocone $\alpha$, [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test] says that $q$ is a $p$-colimit diagram if and only if, for every $z$, its square is a homotopy pullback. The lower row of that square is a map between copies of $\Delta^0$, since $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^0)=\Delta^0$ and each right-pinched mapping space of $\Delta^0$ has one simplex in each degree; the path-pullback model is then the upper-right corner itself. So the condition says that $u\mapsto\Delta_K(u)\alpha$, $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(f,\Delta_Kz)$, is an equivalence for every $z$, which by the cocone dual of the mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that $\alpha$ is colimiting. This translation is used in both directions below, for $\mathcal C=\mathcal P(D)$ and $\mathcal C=Z$. Choose a $\mathcal U$-small quasicategory $R$ and an equivalence $e:R\simeq A_{/F}$. The maps from $\mathcal P(D)$ and $Z$ to $\Delta^0$ are inner fibrations, since their inner-horn lifting conditions are exactly the quasicategory conditions. By [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](2), with the target map $\mathcal P(D)\to\Delta^0$, the cocone $\delta_Fe^{\triangleright}$ is colimiting. All its vertices are in $E$, so it factors through $E$. Applying $H$ makes this small cocone colimiting in $Z$ by the hypothesis on $H$. Apply the same equivalence-invariance statement with target map $Z\to\Delta^0$ to conclude that $(H|_E)$ applied to the entire canonical cocone on $A\times_E E_{/c}$ is colimiting. This uses small colimit preservation only for the diagram indexed by $R$; it requires no colimit closure of $E$ and no property of $G$.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.3, printed p. 325, and the forward direction of Lemma 5.1.5.5(1), printed pp. 326-327; equality of full-subcategory slices is checked degree by degree.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] with source quasicategory $E$, full subcategory $A$, target $Z$, first functor $H|_E$ and second functor $G$. Step 2 supplies its colimit hypothesis at every object of $E$, so restriction gives an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(E,Z)}(H|_E,G)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,Z)}(H|_A,G|_A).$$
The comparison is the actual restriction map and is coherent in all parameters by that node.

source.place: Corollary 7.3.6.9, applied to the representable full subcategory of E

proof.text: Work in the containing universe $\mathcal W$ chosen in step 1. Let $J:D\to A$ be the factorization of $y_E$ from step 1. Precomposition defines $J^*:\operatorname{Fun}(A,Z)\to\operatorname{Fun}(D,Z)$ and $K^*$ in the reverse direction. Whiskering the unit and counit of [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] gives coherent transformations $J^*K^*\simeq1$ and $K^*J^*\simeq1$: their components are obtained by applying each functor to the unit or counit equivalence. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes these equivalences in the functor categories, and its mapping-space clause makes $J^*$ induce an equivalence on the right-hand mapping space of step 3. The composite with restriction to $A$ is restriction along $y_E$ itself. In degree $n$, both composites precompose a map $E\times\Delta^n\to Z$ with $y_E\times1$; this equality also holds with every further simplex parameter. Thus it commutes with changes in $H,G$ and with restriction to another intermediate full subcategory. The homotopy fiber over any transformation $Hy\to Gy_E$ is contractible because the restriction map is an equivalence of spaces. Taking the transformation given by the stated identification with $Gy_E$ gives the final comparison. Functor categories are formed in a sufficiently large containing universe, so this argument places no $\mathcal U$-smallness requirement on $E$.

source.place: Functor equivalence and mapping-space calculus, Proposition 1.2.7.3 and Section 1.2.10; the precise statements used are lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image and lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus. Degreewise restriction verifies the stated naturality.

lean.statement: theorem intermediate_presheaf_kan (D : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory D] (P : (intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D) _⦋0⦌ → Prop) (hreplete : ∀ e : (intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D) _⦋1⦌, IsEquivalenceEdge (intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D) e → (P ((intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D).δ 1 e) ↔ P ((intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D).δ 0 e))) (hy : Subcomplex.range (intermediatePresheafYoneda.{u, v} D) ≤ fullSubcomplex (intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D) P) (Z : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [Quasicategory Z] (hZ : ∀ I : SSet.{u}, HasInfinityColimitsOfShape (SSet.uliftFunctor.{max (u + 1) v, u}.obj I) Z) (H : intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D ⟶ Z) (hH : ∀ I : SSet.{u}, PreservesInfinityColimitsOfShape (SSet.uliftFunctor.{max (u + 1) v, u}.obj I) H) (G : (fullSubcomplex (intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D) P).toSSet ⟶ Z) : IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (intermediatePresheafMappingRestriction D P hy H G) ∧ (∀ b, IsContractible (homotopyFiber (intermediatePresheafMappingRestriction D P hy H G) b)) ∧ (∀ (K : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) (T : K ⟶ (ihom (fullSubcomplex (intermediatePresheafAmbient D) P).toSSet).obj Z), MonoidalClosed.uncurry (T ≫ intermediatePresheafRestriction D P hy Z) = intermediateYoneda D P hy ▷ K ≫ MonoidalClosed.uncurry T) ∧ (∀ (Q : (intermediatePresheafAmbient.{u, v} D) _⦋0⦌ → Prop) (hQP : fullSubcomplex (intermediatePresheafAmbient D) Q ≤ fullSubcomplex (intermediatePresheafAmbient D) P) (hyQ : Subcomplex.range (intermediatePresheafYoneda.{u, v} D) ≤ fullSubcomplex (intermediatePresheafAmbient D) Q), (MonoidalClosed.pre (Subcomplex.homOfLE hQP)).app Z ≫ intermediatePresheafRestriction D Q hyQ Z = intermediatePresheafRestriction D P hy Z)
